candidates.name: TITAN CORE
risk_notes: Repository created recently (November 2026); provenance and source commit audit pending
Bundles and automatically loads kstuff-lite and ShadowMountPlus; possible conflict with existing autoload
Release ELF byte-for-byte independent SHA-256 not verified
User reports include game compatibility issues
required_before_promotion: Pin and audit public source commit and build provenance
Download exact ELF and independently calculate SHA-256
Verify firmware 13.60 compatibility and developer identity
Confirm CI green and no duplicate/unsafe boot behavior
candidates.independent_report: MODDED WARFARE, 2026-11-21: Install and Run Fake Packages up to 13.60 with TitanCore
candidates.review_note: Upstream release ELF SHA256 metadata present; independent byte download blocked by network DNS in verification environment. No static code audit completed. Do not promote.

findings: Upstream documentation claims 104 synthetic Rust tests and two successful ELF build stages; independently unverified
Pinned vendor kstuff-lite v1.11 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta10 are embedded as release binaries, not rebuilt from source
Maintainer explicitly says no new v1.0 hardware acceptance test and no universal firmware/game compatibility
External PKG system storage accounting unresolved
Public report disputes bundled service startup reliability; needs reproduction
Local verification environment cannot resolve github.com; exact ELF bytes and independent SHA-256 unavailable
Confirmed upstream CI success for pinned source commit; release asset reproducibility not established
audit.source_review_scope: documentation and CI workflow only; no complete static audit or binary verification

upstream_ci.note: Upstream CI success is not DK catalog promotion CI and does not establish ELF provenance or safety.

findings: Boot path checks firmware and refuses outside 1.00–13.60; source-level check does not prove real hardware compatibility
Boot may write embedded ShadowMountPlus/kstuff ELFs under /data/titan-core/payloads and dispatch them, rather than operating as a passive UI
Existing ready services are reused; inconsistent ShadowMount-ready/kstuff-not-ready state blocks reload
One startup-attempt marker per boot and 90-second readiness deadline; no automatic retry on uncertain dispatch
Existing service detection can still be imperfect; requires explicit opt-in and hardware validation for user's existing payload chain
code_review.decision: NO-GO for automatic catalog promotion; embedded kernel payload dispatch needs special risk acceptance and independent binary verification
